statement: A worker must never poll or sleep for deferred external conditions (CI checks, dependency completion, time-based delays); instead it publishes a `waiting` status with a structured `.sergeant-wake-condition` file naming one of six supported condition kinds, then exits cleanly, and the scheduler resumes it automatically once the condition is met.

source.quote:
Do not use sleep or polling loops for deferred work such as CI checks, dependency completion, or time-based delays. Use the `waiting` status with a structured wake condition instead: write `.sergeant-wake-condition` with a supported `kind` and the required fields, set `.sergeant-status=waiting`, then exit the session cleanly. The Sergeant scheduler (`sgt-wake`) evaluates the condition and resumes the session automatically when it is met.

Supported wake condition kinds and their required fields:

trigger: a worker's next step depends on an external asynchronous event
outcome: no worker process (and its billed harness turn) sits idle burning resources; the runtime durably tracks the deferred condition and resumes deterministically
notes: This is exactly the needs_input/waiting semantics the proposal (§8.2, §15.4) flags as a rich source of engine-pressure findings; tests/sgt-wake-test.sh exercises the six condition kinds end-to-end.
rationale: Lower rungs tried: (1) helper script that polls in a loop — rejected explicitly by this same text as the anti-pattern; (2) actor-stage judgment call — a worker cannot itself durably survive process exit while 'waiting', so judgment alone cannot own the resumption guarantee.
alternatives_considered: helper (polling loop) — explicitly prohibited by source
actor stage with judgment — cannot survive process exit

engine_gap.behavior: A workflow must be able to suspend indefinitely on an external condition (time, CI check, another fleet task, a td dependency, a deployment, or a human response) and be durably, deterministically resumed when that condition becomes true, without any process polling in the interim.
engine_gap.source_evidence: templates/worker-brief.md ('waiting' status + six wake-condition kinds) and tests/sgt-wake-test.sh (sgt-wake scheduler seam).
lower_rungs_attempted: workflow-local helper script that loops/sleeps until the condition holds
actor-stage judgment (the actor decides when to resume itself)
engine_gap.why_each_fails: A polling helper burns a live process and a billed turn for an indefinite, sometimes multi-day span, and cannot survive a daemon or host restart. An actor cannot resume itself after its own process exits; only the runtime, which owns durable Work state independent of process state, can evaluate a condition and re-enter a stage later.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: A first-class 'waiting' stage/status the engine can persist across restarts, plus a small set of runtime-evaluated condition predicates (time, external check, intra-fleet dependency) that trigger stage re-entry without any actor process running meanwhile.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: A workflow stage publishes a wait condition, its process exits, the daemon restarts, and when the condition later becomes true the stage resumes automatically with no polling process ever observed running in between.
